title: the birth
hook: at midnight in a dark prison, a child appears with four arms, and his mother asks him to look like an ordinary baby
carry: he becomes small enough to hold

segments.voice: Yesterday, before the birth: Balarama moved in secret to Rohini, Devaki shining in the prison, the gods singing to a child not yet born. Your line was the gods come to sing. What good thing did you leave alone to grow? Day eight hundred eighty-one.

The Bhagavata sets the scene slowly, as if it doesn't want to rush the night. The sky is clear. The rivers run clean. Lotuses open on the lakes, and birds and bees fill the woods with sound. A cool, fragrant breeze moves. The sacred fires of the brahmanas burn bright and steady. And in the middle of the night, in deep darkness, inside a locked cell in Mathura, the text says the Lord appeared from Devaki the way the full moon rises in the east. Today, the moment the whole story has been waiting for.
screen: `A CLEAR SKY, CLEAN RIVERS.` → `MIDNIGHT, DEEP DARKNESS.` → `LIKE THE FULL MOON RISING.`

segments.voice: Vasudeva looks at the newborn, and it is not an ordinary baby. The child has four arms, holding a conch, a mace, a discus and a lotus. A jewel shines at his throat. He wears yellow silk. Vasudeva knows exactly who this is. He folds his hands and praises him: you are the one beyond all things, and you have come into this house. Then Devaki speaks. Her praise is lovely, and then it turns very practical, very much a mother's. Please, she says, hide this form. Kamsa must not know you have been born here. And this shape, with the conch and discus, is too much for ordinary eyes. Become small. The Lord answers by telling them a secret. He has been their child before. In an earlier age, he says, they spent long years in austerity, asking for a son like him, and he was born to them. Then again in another life. Now this is the third time. Remember me as your son, he tells them, and you will reach me. And then, while they watch, he does what his mother asked. The four arms, the jewel, the radiance: gone. On the prison floor there is a newborn, like any other. That is the heart of the birth in this telling. The Lord of the universe arrives at full height, and the first thing he does, at his mother's request, is make himself small enough to be held and hidden. In this telling, the childhood stories to come, the butter, the mischief, the cowherds, grow out of that one choice.
screen: `FOUR ARMS, CONCH AND DISCUS` · `DEVAKI: PLEASE, HIDE THIS FORM` · `"I HAVE BEEN YOUR CHILD BEFORE"` · then, large: `HE BECOMES AN ORDINARY BABY`

segments.voice: Sit, and let the room grow quiet. In this story, what is greatest becomes small enough to hold. Let your hands rest loosely in your lap. Breathe in, and bring to mind one small, ordinary thing in your day that you could treat as precious: a cup of tea, a child's voice, a friend's message. Breathe out, and let it be enough. If you pray, you can offer that small thing in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
The birth. At midnight in a prison the Lord appears in full glory, and at his mother's request becomes a baby.
Your line: he becomes small enough to hold. Today, treat one small, ordinary moment as if something great had chosen to hide inside it. Day eight hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Hindus celebrate Krishna's birth at Janmashtami, and in homes and temples some devotees keep watch until midnight, the hour the Bhagavata gives for the birth, and then celebrate.
